nodes.name: Fe-doped cobalt hydroxide synthesis
nodes.procedure: Fe–Co(OH)2 synthesized by Fe3+ substitution into Co(OH)2 lattice (spontaneous, negative formation energy) due to similar ionic radii Fe3+ (55 pm) vs Co2+ (65 pm), forming sheet-like morphology with lattice spacing 2.4 Å (011 planes), increased oxygen vacancies.
nodes.source_text: high concentration of Fe can be attributed to the formative CoFe hydroxide due to similar ionic radii of Fe3+ (55 pm) and Co2+ (65 pm)... DFT calculations reveal that the substitution of Co sites with Fe is a spontaneous process with a negative formation energy... Fe–Co(OH)2 component exhibits distinct lattice spacings with an interplanar distance of 2.4 Å, corresponding to the (011) planes

nodes.name: CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 heterostructure synthesis
nodes.procedure: CeO2/Fe–Co(OH)2 heterojunction formed by depositing low-crystallinity spherical CeO2 nanoparticles onto sheet-like Fe–Co(OH)2, creating abundant sheet-sphere interfaces (formation energy -2.34 eV), Co:Fe:Ce = 4.41:1.14:1 (ICP), work function Δφ = 0.99 eV drives electron transfer.

unit_operations.name: Nanoparticle deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: CeO2 with low crystallinity forms heterostructures with Fe–Co(OH)2

nodes.source_text: scalable strategy... introducing valence state tunable rare earth oxide Ceδ+O_x on Fe doped cobalt–iron hydroxide Fe–Co(OH)2 to form a CeO2/Fe–Co(OH)2 heterojunction... formation energy of the CeO2/Fe–Co(OH)2 heterostructure is −2.34 eV... ICP results reveal that the Co:Fe:Ce ratio is about 4.41:1.14:1

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH using three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: To elucidate the effects of interface engineering and Fe doping on the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Co-based catalysts, this study comprehensively evaluates the electrochemical behavior of the synthesized samples in 1 M KOH. As shown in Fig. 4a, CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 exhibits the highest OER activity... At current densities of 10 mA cm−2, 500 mA cm−2 and 1000 mA cm−2, the overpotentials for CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 are measured to be 189, 309, and 346 mV, respectively. The Tafel slope of CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 is calculated to be 39 mV dec−1... CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 demonstrates an impressive faradaic efficiency approaching 100%. Furthermore, CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 exhibits remarkable stability, operating stably for 800 hours at 1 A
As shown in Fig. 4a, CeO2/Co(OH)2... both of which surpass the performance of commercial RuO2 and Fe-Co(OH)2
As shown in Fig. 4a, CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 exhibits the highest OER activity, followed by CeO2/Co(OH)2, both of which surpass the performance of commercial RuO2 and Fe-Co(OH)2

nodes.description: AEMWE performance achieving 1000 mA/cm2 at 1.78 V
nodes.source_text: Remarkably, the constructed CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 catalyst demonstrates outstanding activity (189 and 346 mV at 10 and 1000 mA cm−2) and viable durability (800 h at 1000 mA cm−2), achieving 1000 mA cm−2 at 1.78 V for 1600 h in practical AEMWE setups... the long-term stability of the AEMWEs is maintained beyond 1600 hours

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 shows sheet-like Fe-Co(OH)2 and spherical CeO2 particles with abundant interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: FE-SEM images reveal that Fe-Co(OH)2 and CeO2 are typical sheet-like and spherical particles, respectively. The CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 catalyst shows distinct sheet-like and spherical morphologies, with abundant interface density.

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 interface shows Fe-Co(OH)2 lattice spacing of 2.4 Å (011) planes of Co(OH)2; CeO2 amorphous.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM images display local heterostructures... Fe-Co(OH)2 component exhibits distinct lattice spacings with an interplanar distance of 2.4 Å, corresponding to the (011) planes of Co(OH)2.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM mapping reveals uniform distribution of Co, Fe, and O elements, while Ce is exclusively localized within brighter particulate regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM mapping in Fig. 2g and Fig. S2c, d (ESI†) reveals a uniform distribution of Co, Fe, and O elements, while Ce is exclusively localized within these brighter particulate regions.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP results reveal Co : Fe : Ce ratio of about 4.41 : 1.14 : 1 in CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma (ICP) results of CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 reveal that the Co : Fe : Ce ratio is about 4.41 : 1.14 : 1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Only Co(OH)2 phase observed for CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 catalyst; diffraction peaks shift slightly to higher angles confirming Fe incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is consistent with the XRD results in Fig. S3a (ESI†), where only the Co(OH)2 phase is observed for the CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra exhibit stretching vibrational peaks at 454 and 524 cm⁻¹ (A1g and A2u modes of Co(OH)2) and Ce–O bond vibration at 463 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the Raman spectra of CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 in Fig. S3b (ESI†) exhibit two distinct stretching vibrational peaks at 454 and 524 cm⁻¹, which are attributed to the A1g and A2u modes of Co(OH)2, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR analysis shows Fe-Co(OH)2 contains more substantial amount of oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) analysis aligned with the DFT result that the synthesized Fe-Co(OH)2 contains a more substantial amount of oxygen vacancies (Fig. 2k).

nodes.characterization_summary: CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 shows Co2+/Co3+ shift to higher binding energy vs Fe-Co(OH)2; Ce3+/Ce4+ coexist; Fe2+/Fe3+ present; O1s peaks at 533.2 eV (Oads), 531.8 eV (Ov), 530.6 eV (Oh), 529.1 eV (M-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ce 3d XPS spectrum displays the coexistence of Ce3+ and Ce4+... The Fe 2p spectrum indicates the presence of both Fe3+ and Fe2+. In the O 1s spectrum... characteristic peaks at 533.2 eV, 531.8 eV, 530.6 eV, and 529.1 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Work functions determined as 2.92 eV for CeO2 and 1.93 eV for Fe-Co(OH)2, ΔΦ = 0.99 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated Φ values for CeO2 and Fe-Co(OH)2 are 2.92 eV and 1.93 eV, respectively, indicating a substantial ΔΦ of 0.99 eV at their interface (Fig. 3f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 has higher energy absorption edge than Fe-Co(OH)2, indicating higher average Co valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the XANES Co K-edge spectra (Fig. 3h), both CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 and Fe-Co(OH)2 exhibit spectral line shapes similar to Co(OH)2 indicating that Co predominantly exists in the Co(OH)2 form.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-Co(OH)2 shows Co–O at 1.63 Å and Co–O–Co/Fe at 2.66 Å; CeO2/Fe-Co(OH)2 shows only Co–O coordination at 1.58 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the EXAFS spectra (Fig. 3i), Fe-Co(OH)2 exhibits two prominent peaks at 1.63 Å and 2.66 Å, corresponding to Co–O and Co–O–Co/Fe interactions, respectively.
